ogTitle: Where to Stay in Thong Lo–Ekkamai, Bangkok
ogDesc: The best hotels in Thong Lo–Ekkamai by budget.
intro: Thong Lo–Ekkamai is the Sukhumvit stretch around Soi 38–63 that locals call Bangkok's coolest district, packed with Japanese restaurants, cafés, and late-night bars. Two BTS stations, Thong Lo (Soi 55) and Ekkamai (Soi 63), make it easy to eat and drink here and still get into the city.

blocks.html: Short answer: Thong Lo–Ekkamai (Sukhumvit Soi 38–63) is for people who come to eat, café-hop, and drink late in Bangkok's trendiest district. BTS Thong Lo and Ekkamai both run into town, and Japanese restaurants and bars are within walking distance. Rates start around ฿900 for a guesthouse and climb past ฿6,000 for the 5-star towers.

items.name: Lodge 61 Hotel
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Budget · by Ekkamai BTS · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A small B&B on Sukhumvit Soi 61 next to Major Cineplex Ekamai, a few minutes' walk from Ekkamai BTS and the Eastern Bus Terminal. Rooms are simple and some have a balcony. Reviews call it good value, though a few mention the fittings are a bit dated. Good if you just want a clean bed near the train.

items.name: 63 Bangkok Boutique Residence Ekamai
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Budget · short stays by the station · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: Right by the Ekkamai BTS exit, basically across the street, so it's handy if you arrive with luggage and want to drop straight in. Rooms are compact boutique-style. Ratings are middling and management has changed over the years, so check recent reviews before booking, but the location is hard to beat at this price.

items.name: Somerset Sukhumvit Thonglor Bangkok
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Families · longer self-catering stays · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A serviced apartment on Soi Thonglor with in-room kitchens and washer/dryers, suited to families or multi-night stays. There's an outdoor pool and a free tuk-tuk shuttle to Thong Lo BTS, which helps because the building sits a fair way down the soi. Guests praise the spacious, clean units.

items.name: MUU Bangkok (formerly Akyra Thonglor)
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Couples · design-boutique fans · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A small Small Luxury Hotels boutique on Soi Thonglor. The draw is a twin rooftop infinity pool with 180-degree city views. Rooms feel like a high-end apartment, with contemporary artwork, and it's quieter than the streets around it. A good fit for couples who want a stylish, low-key stay.

items.name: Grande Centre Point Sukhumvit 55
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Families · onsen and spa lovers · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A large tower on Sukhumvit Soi 55 by the Thong Lo BTS, with a rooftop infinity pool, a kids' club, and a whole floor of Let's Relax onsen and spa. It holds a 2026 Travellers' Choice award. A solid pick for families who want everything in one building and enjoy a Japanese-style onsen soak.

items.name: Hotel Nikko Bangkok
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Couples · fans of Japanese-style service · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A Japanese hotel on Sukhumvit Soi 55, about a 2-minute walk to Thong Lo BTS, with TOTO Washlet toilets in every room. Guests repeatedly praise the breakfast buffet and the gym, and it ranks among the top hotels in Bangkok by review score. Great for travellers who like Japanese-style service and a quiet, comfortable room.

items.name: Bangkok Marriott Hotel Sukhumvit
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Luxury · rooftop-bar lovers · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A 5-star hotel a 2–3 minute walk from Thong Lo BTS. The headline is Octave, a multi-level rooftop bar on floors 45–49 with 360-degree city views. Rooms are modern with bathtubs, the review scores are high, and it's the top-end choice in the area. A good fit if you want both a great location and a famous rooftop scene.

faq.q: What's the difference between Thong Lo and Ekkamai, and where should I stay?
faq.a: The two areas sit side by side on Sukhumvit and are walkable to each other. Thong Lo (Soi 55) leans toward Japanese restaurants, cafés, and upscale bars, while Ekkamai (Soi 63) is a touch more laid-back with more budget-friendly stays. Pick Thong Lo for higher-end eating and drinking, Ekkamai to keep costs down.

faq.q: Is it easy to get into the city from here?
faq.a: Yes. Two BTS stations, Thong Lo and Ekkamai, sit on the Sukhumvit line, with a straight ride to Asok for the MRT or on to Siam. Note that some hotels are deep inside the soi, so you may need a motorbike taxi or the hotel shuttle to reach the main road first.

faq.q: Is Thong Lo–Ekkamai good for families with kids?
faq.a: It can be, if you choose the right hotel. The area is known for bars and nightlife, but there are family-friendly options with pools and kids' clubs, like Grande Centre Point Sukhumvit 55, or serviced apartments such as Somerset with in-room kitchens that suit families cooking for themselves on longer stays.
